title: Class Bravo transition: the magic words

briefing.description: You want to fly straight through the Class Bravo instead of the long way around. One iron rule governs this flight: you may not enter Bravo airspace until you hear the literal words “CLEARED INTO/THROUGH THE CLASS BRAVO AIRSPACE”. Two-way contact isn't enough. “Radar contact” isn't enough. Sometimes the answer is “remain clear” — and you wait.

steps.text: Level at 3,500, the Bravo shelf starts five miles ahead. Call BEFORE the boundary — with enough time to turn away if the answer is no.

steps.prompt: Call Metro Approach: who/where/altitude, and request the Bravo transition northbound.
steps.hint: Metro Approach, Skyhawk {callsign}, one five miles south of Metro at three thousand five hundred, request transition through the Class Bravo, northbound.

elements.label: your position
elements.feedbackMissing: Give your position: “one five miles south of Metro”.

elements.label: your altitude
elements.feedbackMissing: State your altitude — they need it to fit you under the arrivals.
elements.feedbackWrong: You said {heard} feet, but you're level at 3,500.

elements.label: the transition request
elements.expected: request transition through the class bravo
elements.feedbackMissing: Make the request explicitly: “request transition through the Class Bravo”.

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, Metro Approach, squawk {squawk} — and remain clear of the Class Bravo for now, I have arrivals crossing your route.

steps.prompt: The answer for now is NO. Read back the squawk AND the remain-clear instruction — then actually stay out.
steps.hint: Squawk {squawk}, remaining clear of the Class Bravo, Skyhawk {callsign}.

elements.label: squawk readback
elements.feedbackWrong: You read back {heard}, but the assigned squawk is {squawk}.

elements.label: remain-clear readback
elements.expected: remaining clear of the class bravo
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back “remaining clear of the Class Bravo” — this is the instruction that keeps you legal. Entering now would be a violation.

steps.text: You start a lazy 360 outside the shelf, transponder flashing your new code. Two airliners slide past above. Then:

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, radar contact. Cleared through the Class Bravo airspace, maintain three thousand five hundred, fly heading three six zero.

steps.prompt: There they are — the magic words. Read back the Bravo clearance, the altitude, and the heading.
steps.hint: Cleared through the Class Bravo, maintain three thousand five hundred, heading three six zero, Skyhawk {callsign}.

elements.label: the Bravo clearance readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the clearance itself: “cleared through the Class Bravo”. This is the one phrase in VFR flying where the exact words legally matter.

elements.label: altitude readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the assigned altitude — inside Bravo, altitude assignments are binding.
elements.feedbackWrong: You read back {heard} feet, but the assignment is 3,500.

elements.label: heading readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the heading: “heading three six zero”.

steps.text: You cruise through the Bravo, the big airport sliding beneath your wings — heavies on the parallels, and you, a Skyhawk, right through the middle. Perfectly legal, because you heard the words.

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, you are leaving the Class Bravo airspace to the north. Radar services terminated, squawk VFR, frequency change approved. Good day.

steps.hint: Squawk VFR, frequency change approved, Skyhawk {callsign}. Good day.

elements.label: squawk VFR acknowledgment
elements.feedbackMissing: Acknowledge “squawk VFR” — confirm you'll reset to 1200.

steps.text: Transition complete. Remember the rule that made it work: no entry without “cleared into/through the Class Bravo” — and when the answer is “remain clear”, you wait like a pro.
